answer: Memory-hard working-set audits make each seat keep its own RAM busy. A seat derives a 2 GB table from its key with a sequential cipher, and at random moments the network quizzes hundreds of seats at once for 64 table entries, due within 3 seconds. Rebuilding a table takes about 40 seconds, so only a seat holding it resident passes. An honest seat, say one pricing marble slabs or forecasting orchard frost, pays 2 GB once; a farm of 500 fakes must keep 1 TB live at the same instant. Sharing one table fails, since every key yields a different table, and paging to disk misses the deadline.
